recorded_prior_demo_execution.note: These are historical run results, not a new execution in this audit.

observations.evidence: patches appends (r,c,value), and in_patch unpacks exactly those three fields. Pair selection initially treats index 2 as color, then accesses indices 3 and 4. paint unpacks four bounds and reads color at index 5. The later intersection instead assumes indices 0..3 are row/column bounds.
observations.implication: The historical tuple IndexError is real, but there is no single consistent pre-existing rectangle schema to recover by padding the tuple. Record construction, color selectors, geometry and painting require coordinated semantic choices.

observations.evidence: A cell is rejected if an orthogonal neighbor has the same color. Demo 0 contains eight 2x2 colored cores inside separate containers: every core cell has same-color neighbors and is rejected. Its separated legend pixels satisfy the isolation predicate and are retained because the extraction does not exclude the legend row.
observations.implication: Fixing record length cannot recover missing rectangular colored objects or their spans. A bbox over a retained singleton is insufficient to represent demo 0 objects.

observations.evidence: The code takes one row range per color across the whole grid and requires that color in every intervening row. The separated frame rows in these demos include blank inter-object rows, so the frame color cannot become separate container records through this code. Membership checks compare an integer color to whole tuples (including a comprehension that returns those same tuples), and patches are appended without reference to a container.
observations.implication: The intended distinction between container extent and inner colored payload is absent from the actual representation, rather than merely misplaced in one tuple field.

observations.evidence: paint names s1/s2 as the second object row bounds and t1/t2 as its column bounds, but its vertical branches compare the first object row bounds with t1/t2 and use them to derive vertical row ranges. The pairing block also mixes positional fields that cannot share the color and bbox interpretations used elsewhere.
observations.implication: Even after making tuples long enough, axis and field semantics remain wrong; successful execution would not establish the intended connection rule.

observations.evidence: After one selected pair, both endpoints are marked used and excluded from every later legend pair. Demo 2 explicitly requires the top-middle colored object to participate in both the preceding and following connection (the legend starts 3,2,9). One object therefore has to be reusable as a destination and later a source.
observations.implication: The selection state implements disjoint pairs, while the demonstrated relation includes a chain. Repairing that state is a rule/selection change beyond tuple-length correction.

conclusion: The cheaper DeepP0 output loses the object representation, field contract and connection semantics in multiple places. This source does not support the claim that a single mechanical tuple fix would recover the correct rule or save the longer direct-generation budget. A coherent rewrite would become a manually developed solver, not a clean test of isolated representation repair.
decision: Stop manual candidate and Notebook preparation for this case; retain this source audit only. No candidate or new full solution was created.
limitations: Static deductions are grounded in existing source and known demos; no repaired behavior was measured.
The task was selected after parent reported an outcome difference, so any later manual development on it would be a diagnostic development case, not independent generalization evidence.
No inference about query correctness is made from these observations.
